en: *The Brief Compilation of the Kaiyuan Era Catalogue of Buddhist Teachings*, Volume One.

Compiled by the Śramaṇa Zhisheng of Chongfu Monastery in the Western Regions during the Tang Dynasty. [This volume contains] the *Bodhisattvapiṭaka Tripiṭaka*. [Recorded during] the third year of the Gengwu year of the Southern Canon.

The Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra, six hundred fascicles, translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang at the Yuhua Palace Monastery during the Tang Dynasty; sixty bundles, totaling ten thousand six hundred and forty-nine sheets. From the character 【天】 (Tian) to the character 【柰】 (Nai).

The *Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra* (Fàngguāng bōrě bōluómì jīng), thirty fascicles, translated by the Western Jin Tripiṭaka Master Mokṣala together with Zhu Shulan; totaling six hundred and twenty-six sheets. [Characters: 菜, 重, 芥].

The Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra, thirty fascicles, also titled the Dapin Prajñā Sūtra, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty together with Sengrui and others; totaling four hundred and eighty-three sheets. [Jiāng] [Hǎi] [Xián].

*The Sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā Praised by Light*, ten fascicles, translated by the Tripitaka Master Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin. *The Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, five fascicles—also known as the "Subhūti Chapter" or the "Chang'an Chapter"—translated by the Indian Śramaṇa Dhammapiya (Tanmopi) together with Zhu Fonian of the Fu Qin. These two sūtras comprise fifteen fascicles in two bundles, totaling three hundred and thirteen sheets. [He] [Dan].

The *Daoxing Banruo Boluomi Jing* (Sūtra on the Practice of the Perfection of Wisdom), ten fascicles; also known as the "Chapter on the Practice of the Way" (*Daoxingpin*). Translated by the Yuezhi Tripiṭaka Master Zhi Loujiachen of the Later Han Dynasty. This single volume comprises one hundred and seventy-one sheets. [Lín].

The *Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra in Small Chapters*, ten fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty; comprising one bundle, totaling one hundred and sixty-two sheets. [Qian].

*Mahāprajñāpāramitā-sūtra* (The Sutra of the Great Perfection of Wisdom), six fascicles; also titled *Damingdu jing*. Translated by the Yuezhi lay devotee Zhi Qian of the Wu dynasty. *Jinwang tian banruo boluomi jing* (The Sutra of the Prajñāpāramitā of the Victorious Heavenly King), seven fascicles. Translated by Prince Śubhakaravarman of the kingdom of Ujjayinī during the Chen dynasty. These two sutras comprise thirteen fascicles in one volume, totaling two hundred twenty-one pages. [Section Yu].
*The Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra Spoken by Mañjuśrī*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Mandarakaśyapa of Funan during the Liang dynasty.

*The Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra Spoken by Mañjuśrī*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Saṃghavarman of Funan during the Liang dynasty. *The Sūtra on the Supreme Pure Almsround of the Bodhisattva Niu-shou*, two fascicles;

translated by the Śramaṇa Shuogong at Nanhai Commandery during the Song dynasty. *The Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty.

*Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, one fascicle, translated by Kumārajīva; *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, one fascicle, translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci during the Northern Wei dynasty;
*Vajracchedikā Prajñāpārmitā Sūtra*, one fascicle, translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha at the Jetavana Monastery during the Chen dynasty;

*Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta during the Daye era of the Sui dynasty; *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang at Śrāvastī in the Tang dynasty.
*Chūn-tien-lu* (Catalogue of Buddhist Scriptures): 1 scroll of the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, translated by the Śramaṇa Yijing during the reign of Empress Wu of the Tang dynasty;

this is the fifth translation, newly included in the catalogue. 1 scroll of the *Bhūtakoṭi-prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci during the reign of Empress Wu of the Tang dynasty.

2 scrolls of the *Ratnaketuparivarta Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* (Renwang Huguo), translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty. 1 scroll of the *Prajñāpāramitā-hṛdaya Sūtra*, [translated] in the Tang dynasty... [text truncated].

*Mahāprajñāpāramitāmahāmantra-sūtra*, one fascicle, translated by Xuanzang of the Tang; *Thirteen Sūtras*, fifteen fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin—these are contained in the same volume, totaling one hundred and ninety-nine sheets. The Ratnakūṭa Section:

The Ratnakūṭa Section comprises eighty-two works in total from the Qin period. The *Mahāratnakūṭa-sūtra*, one hundred and twenty fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of South India and others of the Tang—these are contained in twelve volumes, totaling two thousand forty-seven sheets. [Dragon] [Master] [Fire] [Emperor] [Bird] [Official] [Man] [August] [Beginning] [To] [Create] [Writings] [and] [Characters].

*Mahāvaipulya Triśaraṇa Sūtra*, three fascicles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmakṣema of India during the Northern Liang dynasty. *Amitābha-vyūha Sūtra*, two fascicles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Lokakṣema of Yuezhi during the Later Han dynasty. *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra*, two fascicles; translated by the Yuezhi lay devotee Zhi Qian during the Wu dynasty. *Larger Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra*, two fascicles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Saṃghavarman of India during the Cao Wei dynasty. These four sūtras comprise nine fascicles in one volume, totaling two hundred and ninety pages. [Nai].

*The Sūtra of the Land of Akṣobhya Buddha*, two fascicles; translated by the Yuezhi Tripiṭaka Master Lokakṣema of the Later Han. *The Mahāyāna Sūtra of the Ten Dharmas*, one fascicle; the beginning states that the Buddha was dwelling in Rājagṛha; translated by the Liang-period Funan Tripiṭaka Master Saṃghavarman. *The Sūtra of the Universal Gate*, one fascicle; also titled *The Universal Gate Sūtra*; translated by the Western Jin Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa. *The Sūtra of the Womb*, one fascicle; also known as *The Sūtra on Receiving a Body in the Womb*; translated by the Western Jin Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa. *The Sūtra on the Adornment and Purity of Mañjuśrī’s Buddha-field*, two fascicles; translated by the Western Jin Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa. *The Sūtra of the Dharma Mirror*, one fascicle; translated by the Anxi Upāsaka Anxuan of the Later Han together with the Śramaṇa Yan Fotiao. These six sūtras comprise eight fascicles in a single volume, totaling one hundred and forty-four pages. [Fu].

*Ugraparipṛcchā-sūtra* (The Sutra of Ugra’s Questions on the Bodhisattva Practice), two fascicles; translated by the Western Jin Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa. *Māyāśubhavyākaraṇa-sūtra* (The Sutra of the Illusionist Śubha), one fascicle; translated by the Western Jin Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa. *Vinayaviniścaya-sūtra* (The Sutra of the Determination of Discipline), one fascicle;

all catalogs state it was found at Dunhuang, though the name of the person and the date are not clearly recorded. *Buddhabodhyālambana-viśuddhi-citta-sūtra* (The Sutra of Awakening the Pure Mind), two fascicles;

translated by the Sui Dynasty Indian Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta. *Rājño-ratnakūṭa-sūtra* (The Sutra of King Udāyin), one fascicle; translated by the Western Jin Śramaṇa Dharmakṣema. *Sūmatī-sūtra* (The Sutra of Sumati), one fascicle.
*The Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Sumati*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin;

*The Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Ajātaśatru’s Daughter Āśudā*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin; *The Sūtra of the Girl Vimaladattā*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin.
These nine preceding sūtras comprise ten fascicles in a single volume, totaling one hundred and fifty-one pages.

*The Sūtra of the Girl Vimalā*, one fascicle; translated by the Indian Brahmin Gautama Prajñāruci during the Northern Wei dynasty. *The Sūtra on the Inconceivable Buddha-Sphere Spoken by Mañjuśrī*, two fascicles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci during the Tang dynasty. *The Sūtra of the Three-Word Illusion-like Samādhi Spoken by Queen Śrīmālā*, three fascicles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin dynasty. *The Sūtra of the Questions of the Holy Son of Heaven, King Susthitamati*, three fascicles; translated by the Indian Brahmin Gautama Prajñāruci during the Northern Wei dynasty. This is the third translation [of this work]. [The following seven translations have four missing: *The Sūtra of Prince Śubhavyūha*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin dynasty. *The Sūtra of Prince Saṃbhūta*, one fascicle; according to the *Sengyou Lu*, it was lost in the records of Master Dao’an and its translator is unknown. These six sūtras comprise eleven fascicles in a single volume, totaling one hundred and seventy-five sheets. [Character "Shang"].
*The Sūtra on the Bodhisattva Prajñottara’s Inquiry into Great Skillful Means*, two fascicles;

translated by the Tripitaka Master Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin. *The Mahāyāna Sūtra on the Manifestation of Consciousness*, two fascicles; translated by the Tripitaka Master Divākara of Central India during the Tang dynasty.

*The Mahāyāna Vaipulya Essential Wisdom Sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripitaka Master An Shigao of Parthia during the Later Han. *The Sūtra on the Original Vows Asked by Maitreya Bodhisattva*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripitaka Master [of the] Western Jin.

*The Sūtra on the Sun-Moon Mani Jewel Left by the Buddha*, one fascicle, translated by Zhu Fahu; *The Mahāyāna Sūtra on the Adornment of Jewels*, one fascicle, translated by the Yuezhi Tripiṭaka Master Lokakṣema of the Later Han;
*The Śrīmālādevī Siṃhanāda Ekayāna Mahā-upāya Vaipulya Sūtra*, one fascicle, translated during the Jin dynasty by an anonymous Tripiṭaka Master;
*The Vaiśravaṇaparipṛcchā Sūtra*, two fascicles, translated by the Brahmin Gautama Prajñāruci of the Northern Wei. These eight sūtras comprise eleven fascicles.
This volume consists of one hundred and fifty-eight sheets.

The Mahāsaṃnipāta section comprises twenty-four works in total, totaling one hundred and forty-two fascicles. The *Mahāvaipulya-mahāsaṃnipāta-sūtra* in thirty fascicles was translated at Guzang by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmakṣema of India during the Northern Liang dynasty; it spans four volumes from this collection, totaling eight hundred and forty-nine sheets. [Rank] [Yield] [State] [Possession].

The Mahāvaipulya Mahāsannipāta Sūtra: The Sun-Treasury Chapter, ten fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Narendrayaśas of India during the Sui Dynasty; comprising a total of two hundred and thirteen sheets from one bundle. [Yu]

The Mahāsannipāta-candragarbha-sūtra, ten fascicles, translated by the Tripitaka Master Narendrayaśas of India during the Northern Qi dynasty; this single volume comprises two hundred and twenty-eight sheets. [Tao].

The Mahāyāna Mahāsannipāta Kṣitigarbha Daśacakrakṣepaṇa Sūtra, ten fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang Dynasty; comprising one volume totaling one hundred and seventy-two sheets. [Tang].

*Mahāvaipulya Daśacakrakṣitigarbha Sūtra*, eight fascicles; translator lost. *Mahāsannipāta Sumerugarbha Sūtra*, two fascicles, translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Narendrayaśas together with Fazhi during the Northern Qi dynasty. These two sūtras comprise ten fascicles in one volume, totaling one hundred fifty-three pages. [Diao].

*Ākāśagarbha-bodhisattva-sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Buddhayaśas of Kapiśa during the Yao Qin dynasty. *Ākāśagarbha-bodhisattva-divyamantra-sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmamitra of Kapiśa during the Song dynasty. *Ākāśagarbha-bodhisattva-sūtra*, two fascicles. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta et al. of India during the Sui dynasty. *Sudarśana-ākāśagarbha-bodhisattva-sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmamitra of Kapiśa during the Song dynasty. *Bodhisattva-buddhānusmṛti-samādhi-sūtra*, six fascicles. Translated by the Indian śramaṇa Guṇabhadra together with Xuanchang during the Song dynasty. The above five sūtras comprise eleven fascicles in a single volume, totaling one hundred and sixty-two sheets. [Min].

The Mahāvaipulya Mahāsannipāta Bodhisattva Buddhanusmṛti Samādhi Sūtra, ten fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmagupta of India during the Sui Dynasty; the second translation, comprising one bundle totaling one hundred thirty-eight sheets. [Fa] (Catalogue mark).

*Pratyutpanna Samādhi Sūtra*, three fascicles; translated by the Yuezhi Tripiṭaka Master Lokakṣema during the Later Han Dynasty. *Bhadrapāla Bodhisattva Sūtra*, one fascicle—also known as the *Bhadrapāla Sūtra*; the Sengyou Catalogue states that this is an ancient scripture of Master Dao’an, being an alternative translation of the first four chapters of the *Pratyutpanna Sūtra*. *Mahāvaipulya Mahāsannipāta Bhadrapāla Sūtra*, five fascicles; translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta and others during the Sui Dynasty. These three sūtras comprise nine fascicles in a single volume, totaling one hundred and fifty-five sheets. [ZUI].

*Akṣayamati-nirdeśa Sūtra*, seven fascicles, translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin; *Akṣayamati-bodhisattva Sūtra*, four fascicles, translated by the Śramaṇa Zhìyán of Liangzhou together with Bǎoyún of the Song dynasty. These two sūtras comprise eleven fascicles in one volume, totaling one hundred and eighty-eight sheets. [Zhou].

*Mahāsaṃnipāta-dṛṣṭāntarāja-sūtra*, two fascicles; translated by Jñānagupta and others from India during the Sui dynasty. *Mahākaruṇā-sūtra*, eight fascicles; translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin dynasty. These two sūtras comprise ten fascicles in one volume, totaling one hundred and fifty-five pages. [Fā].

*The Sūtra of the Questions of the Jewel Maiden*, four fascicles, translated by the Tripitaka Master Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin. *The Sūtra of the Silent Youth*, two fascicles, translated by the Tripitaka Master Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin. *The Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Sovereign King*, two fascicles, translated by the Tripitaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin at the Xiaoyao Garden. *The Sūtra of the Questions of the King of Vigorous Prowess*, two fascicles, translated by the Brahmin Gautama Prajñāruci and others of the Northern Wei. These four sūtras comprise ten fascicles in one volume, totaling one hundred and eighty-eight pages. [Yin]
The Ratnaketu Dhāraṇī Sūtra, ten fascicles, translated by the Tripitaka Master Prajñāmitra of India during the Tang Dynasty; this single volume comprises one hundred and thirty-three pages. [Tang]

Avataṃsaka Section: A total of twenty-six works in one hundred and eighty-seven fascicles. *The Great Vaipulya Buddha-avatamsaka Sutra*, fifty fascicles, translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Buddhabhadra and others of the Eastern Jin dynasty; comprising five bundles, totaling one thousand one hundred sheets. [Seated] [Court] [Question] [Path] [Hanging].

The Mahāvaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra, in eighty fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan and others during the reign of Empress Wu Zetian of the Great Tang. Three characters from the Southern Song [catalogue], totaling eight bundles and one thousand three hundred seventy-two sheets. [Gǒng] [Píng] [Zhāng] [Ài] [Yù] [Lí] [Shǒu] [Chén].
*The Scripture on the Dharma-Gate of Entering the Seal through the Power of Faith*, five fascicles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmaruci of India during the Northern Wei dynasty.

*The Scripture on the Adornment of the Wisdom-Light that Transcends the Realms of All Buddhas*, one fascicle; translator lost. *The Scripture on the Inconceivable Realm of the Tathāgata’s Virtuous Wisdom Entered by the Buddha-Flower Adornment*, two fasciles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta et al. of India during the Sui dynasty.

*The Great Vaipulya Scripture on Entering the Inconceivable Wisdom-Virtue of the Tathāgata*, one fascicle; translated by Śikṣānanda of Khotan during the Tang dynasty. *The Great Vaipulya Buddha-Avataṃsaka Scripture*, [incomplete].

*The Section on Contemplating the Buddha’s Sphere*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripitaka Master Tiyun Poye of Khotan during the Tang Dynasty. *The Mahāvaipulya Tathāgata’s Inconceivable Sphere Sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripitaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan during the Tang Dynasty.
*The Section on the Practice of the Bodhisattva Vajramakuṭamaṇi*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci during the Tang Dynasty.

*The Section on Cultivating Loving-kindness from the Mahāvaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripitaka Master Tiyun Poye during the Tang Dynasty. These eight scriptures, totaling thirteen fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

*The Great Vaipulya Sūtra Spoken by Samantabhadra*, one fascicle, totaling two hundred sheets; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan during the Tang dynasty. *Sūtra on Adorning the Bodhicitta*, one fascicle;

translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty. *Vaipulya Sūtra on the Ten Stages of the Bodhisattva*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kiṅkara from the Western Regions together with Tanyao during the Northern Wei dynasty.

*Duṣa jīng* (The Scripture on the Tuṣita Heaven), one fascicle; translated by the Yuezhi Tripiṭaka Master Zhi Loujiachen of the Later Han. *Bōsà běnyè jīng* (The Scripture on the Original Vows and Deeds of Bodhisattvas), one fascicle; translated by the Yuezhi Upāsaka Zhi Qian of the Wu.

*Zhū púsà qiú fó běnyè jīng* (The Scripture on the Original Vows and Deeds of All Bodhisattvas Seeking Buddhahood), one fascicle; translated by the lay believer Nie Daozhen of the Western Jin. *Bōsà shízhù xíngdào pǐn* (The Chapter on the Ten Stages of Practice for Bodhisattvas), one fascicle;

alternatively titled simply *Bōsà shízhù*; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin. *Bōsà shízhù jīng* (The Scripture on the Ten Stages of Bodhisattvas), one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta of the Western Regions during the Eastern Jin.

*The Sūtra on the Gradual Preparation of All-Wise Virtue*, five fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin; the above nine sūtras, totaling thirteen fascicles, are contained in one volume and comprise one hundred and seventy sheets. *The Sūtra of the Ten Stages*, four fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva together with Buddhabhadra of the Yao Qin;

*The Sūtra on the Samādhi Asked for by the Bodhisattvas*, two fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin; *The Sūtra Manifesting the Merits of Boundless Buddha-lands*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang; *The Sūtra of the Appearance of the Tathāgata*, four fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin. The above four sūtras, totaling eleven fascicles, are contained in one volume and comprise two hundred and twenty-three sheets. [Qiāng].

*The Scripture on the Chapter of Transcending the World*, six fascicles, translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin; *The Lomahaṃga Sūtra*, four fascicles, translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Shengjian of the Qifu Qin; *The Continuation of the Chapter on Entering the Dharma Realm from the Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripitaka Master Divākara of Central India during the Tang dynasty. These three scriptures comprise eleven fascicles in a single volume, totaling two hundred and ten sheets. [Xia]

Nirvāṇa Section. Total of six divisions, fifty-eight fascicles. *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra*, forty fascicles. Translated at Guzang by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmakṣema from India during the Northern Liang dynasty. Comprising four bundles, totaling seven hundred and eighty sheets. [Ē] [Yī] [Tǐ] [Shuài].

The *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra*, later translation, "Section on the Cremation," two fascicles. Translated by the śramaṇa Yanabhadra of Puling in Nanhai, Tang China, together with the śramaṇa Huìníng of Tang China at that country; recorded in the *Dàzhōu lù*. *Single-text Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra*, six fascicles. Translated by the śramaṇa Fǎxiǎn of Píngyáng, Eastern Jin, together with Juéxián. The above two sutras comprise eight fascicles in one volume, totaling one hundred and eighty-five sheets. [Bǐn].

*The Vaipulya Parinirvāṇa Sūtra*, two fascicles, translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin; *The Sūtra on the Samādhi of the Four Boys*, three fascicles, translated by the Tripitaka Master Jñānagupta et al. of India during the Sui dynasty; *The Mahākaruṇā Sūtra*, five fascicles, translated by the Tripitaka Master Narendrayaśas of India together with Fazhi of the Northern Qi. These three sūtras comprise ten fascicles in one volume, totaling one hundred and eighty-two pages. [End of Volume] *Gui*.

Various Re-translated Scriptures Outside the Five Great Collections: 273 works in 588 fascicles. *Lalitavistara Sūtra*, 12 fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Divākara of Central India during the Tang Dynasty; recorded in the *Dazhou Catalogue*. This is the fourth translation. *Puyao jing* (Sūtra of Universal Radiance), 8 fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin Dynasty. These two scriptures comprise 20 fascicles in 2 bundles, totaling 371 sheets. [Wang] [Ming].

*Fahua sanmei jing* (Sutra on the Samādhi of the Lotus), one fascicle; translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Zhiyan of Liangzhou during the Song dynasty. *Wuliangyi jing* (Sutra of Immeasurable Meanings), one fascicle; translated by the Śramaṇa Dharmagatayaśas of India during the Southern Qi dynasty. *Satanbunadari jing* (Sutra of the Excellent White Lotus), one fascicle; according to Sengyou’s catalogue, it was lost among the translations attributed to Master Dao’an. *Miaofa lianhua jing* (Sutra of the Lotus Blossom of the Wondrous Dharma), seven fascicles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty. The above four sutras comprise ten fascicles in a single volume, totaling one hundred and ninety sheets. [Feng]
*The Sutra of the Lotus of the True Dharma*, ten fascicles, translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin; totaling one bundle, comprising one hundred and ninety-six sheets.

[Cai] *The Sutra of the Lotus of the Wonderful Law*, eight fascicles, translated by the two Dharma Masters Kumārajīva and Jñānagupta, the Tripitaka Masters from India of the Sui dynasty; and *The Expanded Version of the Vimalakīrti-nirdeśa Sūtra*, three fascicles, translated by the Tripitaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin. These two sutras comprise eleven fascicles in the same bundle, totaling two hundred and thirty-seven sheets. [Shu]

*Vimalakīrtinirdeśa-sūtra*, three fascicles; translated by the Yuezhi layman Zhi Qian of the Wu [Dynasty]. *Vimalakīrti-nirdeśa-sūtra*, six fascicles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang [Dynasty]. *Mahāvaipulya-uṣṇīṣarāja-sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin [Dynasty]. *Mahāyāna-uṣṇīṣarāja-sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by Prince Upaśūna of the Kingdom of Ujjayinī during the Liang [Dynasty]. These four sūtras comprise eleven fascicles in a single volume, totaling one hundred and ninety-six pages. [Section] Bái.

*The Scripture on the Youth Sudarśana*, two fascicles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta of India during the Sui Dynasty, etc. *The Scripture on the Great Compassion White Lotus*, eight fascicles; translator lost. These two preceding scriptures comprise ten fascicles in one volume, totaling two hundred sheets. [Ku]

The *Karunāpuṇḍarīka-sūtra* (The Compassionate White Lotus Sūtra), ten fascicles, translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Dharmakṣema of the Northern Liang dynasty at Guzang; comprising a total of two hundred and three sheets from this single volume. [Section on Food].
The *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra-rāja*, ten fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing of the Tang Dynasty; comprising one bundle, totaling one hundred and fifty-three sheets. [Section]。

The *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-sūtra* in eight fascicles, compiled by the Śramaṇa Baogui of Daxingshan Monastery during the Sui dynasty; and the *Tuṣṭimdhara-paripṛcchā-sūtra* in three fascicles, translated by the Yuezhi Tripiṭaka Master Lokakṣema of the Later Han dynasty. These two sūtras, totaling eleven fascicles, are contained in the same volume and comprise one hundred and eighty-six sheets. [Section: Huà].

*Qishi jing* (Sūtra on the Arising of the World), ten fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta et al. of India during the Sui dynasty—this single volume comprises one hundred seventy-four sheets. [End].

*Brahmacāri-jalaviśuddhi-kalpanā-sūtra* (Sutra on the Brahmin’s Calculation of Purity through Water), translator lost; now appended to the catalog of the Eastern Jin as part of the *Shiyi* (Supplementary Collection). *Duḥkhaskandha-sūtra* (Sutra on the Aggregate of Suffering), also known as the *Skandha-hetuvastu-sūtra*; translator lost; included in the catalog of the Later Han.

*Shiyi bianru shemo nan benjing* (The Supplementary Compilation: The Original Sutra of Śreṇika), one fascicle; translated by the Yuezhi Upāsaka Zhi Qian of the Wu [Dynasty]. *Kuyin yinshi jing* (Sutra on the Causes of the Aggregate of Suffering), one fascicle; translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Faju of the Western Jin. *Lexiang jing* (Sutra on the Perception of Pleasure), one fascicle;

*The Sūtra on the Prediction of the Fruits for Gautamī*, translated by the Upāsaka Zhi Qian of the Later Han (1 scroll);

One fascicle; also titled *The Scripture on the Demon’s Disturbance*. Translated by the Wu-period Yuezhi upāsaka Zhi Qian. The thirty scriptures above comprise thirty fascicles, totaling one hundred and thirty-five pages.

*The Scripture of Rāṣṭrapāla*, one fascicle; also titled *The Scripture of the Arhat Rāṣṭrapāla*. Translated by the Wu-period Yuezhi upāsaka Zhi Qian. *The Scripture of the Son of Śreṇika*, one [fascicle].

*Shujing* (Numerous Sūtras), one fascicle, translated by the Western Jin śramaṇa Zhi Fadu. *Brahmacārin Araḍa’s Questioning of the Honored One on Lineage Sūtra*, one fascicle, translated by the Western Jin śramaṇa Faju.

*Tri-śaraṇa, Pañca-śīla, Compassionate Mind, and Renunciation of Worldly Desires Merit Sūtra*, one fascicle, translated by the Eastern Jin śramaṇa Zhu Tanwulan. *Śūdraka Sūtra*, one fascicle—also titled *The Sūtra of the Elder Śūdraka*; translator lost, now appended to the Eastern Jin catalog;
translated by the Tianzhu Tripiṭaka Master Guṇavidi of the Xiao Qi dynasty. *Sūtra of the Buddha for the Old Woman of Huangzhu Garden*.

*The Brahmin’s Discourse on Studying the Sūtras*, one fascicle; lost in the record of Sengyou, now appended to the Song Record. *The Parable of the Brahma-demon*, one fascicle; translated by the Wu-period Yuezhi upāsaka Zhi Qian. *The Honored Superior Sūtra*, one fascicle;

translated by the Western Jin Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa. *The Parrot Sūtra*, one fascicle—also titled *The Doudiao Sūtra*; translated by the Song-period Indian Tripiṭaka Master Guṇabhadra. *Doudiao Sūtra*, one fascicle;
according to the record of Sengyou, this was a sūtra whose translator was lost during the time of Master Dao’an; now appended to the Western Jin Record. *The Yi Sūtra*, one fascicle; Western Jin.

*Yingfa jing* (Sūtra on Corresponding to the Dharma), one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin. *Nili jing* (Sūtra on Hell), one fascicle; alternatively titled *Anili jing*; translated by the Śramaṇa Zhu Tanwulan of the Western Regions during the Eastern Jin.
*Upāsikā Duōshèjiā jing* (Sūtra of the Female Lay Disciple Duōshèjiā), one fascicle; a scripture whose translator was lost in Sengyou’s catalogue, now appended to the Song catalogue.

lost in the translation records of Saṃghayou, now appended to the Song dynasty records. *The Sūtra of the Arrow Simile*, one fascicle; translator lost, now appended to the Eastern Jin records. *The Sūtra of Universal Dharma-Meaning*, one fascicle; also known as [the *Sūtra of the Great Meaning*].
*The Sūtra on the Practice Endowed with Dharma*, also titled *The First Sūtra of Universal Meaning*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master An Shigao of Parthia during the Later Han;

*Penshen jing* (Sūtra on Dusting the Body), one fascicle; translated by the Western Jin śramaṇa Shi Faju. *Xumotijunü jing* (Sūtra of the Girl Sumati), one fascicle; translated by the Wu Yuezhi upāsaka Zhi Qian.

*Bolamen bisijing* (Sūtra on the Brāhmaṇa Avoiding Death), one fascicle; translated by the Anxi Tripiṭaka Master An Shigao of the Later Han. *Shishi huowufubao jing* (Sūtra on Receiving Fivefold Meritorious Rewards for Offering Food), one fascicle;

also titled *Shiseli jing* (Sūtra on Bestowing Physical Strength) or *Fude jing* (Sūtra on Merit); translator lost, now appended to the Eastern Jin catalogue. *Pinpishuoluo wang yi fo gongyang jing* (Sūtra on King Bimbisāra Visiting the Buddha to Make Offerings), one fascicle; also called *Pinba*.
*The Sūtra on the Six Times a Householder’s Son Leaves Home*, translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Faju of the Western Jin;

*The Aṅgulimālīya Sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by the Western Jin śramaṇa Shi Faju. *The Sūtra of the Malla Shifting the Mountain*, one fascicle—also simply called *The Sūtra of Shifting the Mountain* or *The Sūtra of the Four Unprecedented Events*;

*The Sūtra on the Eleven Contemplations for Recollecting the Tathāgata*, one fascicle—alternatively called *The Twelve Contemplations*; translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Guṇabhadra of the Song dynasty. *The Sūtra on the Four Nirayas*, one fascicle—or...

*The Clouds of the Four Great Hells*, translated by the Western Region Śramaṇa Zhu Tanwulan of the Eastern Jin; *The Sūtra on Anāthapiṇḍada’s Conversion of His Seven Sons*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master An Shigao of Parthia during the Later Han;

it is now appended to the Western Jin records. *The Scripture on Ānanda’s Fellow Students*, one fascicle. also called *Great Mass of Froth in the River*, or *Parable of the Aggregated Froth*; translated by the Śramaṇa Dharmaruci of the Western Regions during the Eastern Jin. *Sūtra on Not Guarding the Mind*, one fascicle; or...

*The Prātimokṣa Sūtra*, one fascicle; issued from the Kāśyapīya school, translated by the Brahman Gautama Prajñāruci of the Northern Wei. *The Dharma of the Ten Precepts for Śrāmaṇeras and their Deportment*, one fascicle; also known as...

*Śrāmaṇera-vidhi* (The Deportment of Śrāmaṇeras), one fascicle; translator lost, now appended to the Eastern Jin catalogue. Alternatively, there is a version with the title *Sūtra*, which is largely identical to the former but with minor differences; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārabuddha of Kasmīra during the Song dynasty.

*Śrāmaṇerikā-prakīrṇaka-śīla-vinaya* (Miscellaneous Precepts for Śrāmaṇerīs), one fascicle; translator lost, now appended to the Eastern Jin catalogue. *Śrāmaṇerikā-śīla-sūtra* (Sūtra on the Precepts for Śrāmaṇerīs), one fascicle; translator lost, listed in the Later Han catalogue.

*Śāriputra-paripṛcchā-sūtra* (Sūtra of Śāriputra’s Questions), one fascicle; translator lost. These ten sūtras, totaling ten fascicles, are contained in the same volume and comprise one hundred and seventy-two sheets.
*Mūlasarvāstivāda-ekottara-karmavastu*, ten fascicles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing of the Tang Dynasty; comprising one bundle, totaling one hundred and fifty-one sheets. [Fu].

*The One Hundred and One Karmavācanās of the Great Śramaṇa*, one fascicle. Extracted from the *Sarvāstivāda-vinaya*; listed in Sengyou’s catalogue as a work of lost translation, now appended to the Song dynasty catalogues.

*The Essential Karmavācanās for Bhikṣus according to the Sarvāstivāda-vinaya*, one fascicle. Extracted from the *Sarvāstivāda-vinaya* by the Song dynasty śramaṇa Shi Sengqu at Zhongxing Temple in Yangdu.

*The Scripture on Upāli’s Questions to the Buddha*, one fascicle. Also known as the *Upāli-vinaya*. Lost translation; included in the Later Han dynasty catalogues. *The Pañcavargika-karmavācanā*, one fascicle. Titled the *Mūlasarvāstivāda-karmavācanā*; translated during the Tang dynasty.

*The Miscellaneous Karmavācanās of the Four-Part [Vinaya]* (Sifen zajiemo), one fascicle, compiled by the Śramaṇa Shi Aitong of Dàkāiyè Monastery; titled *The Miscellaneous Karmavācanās of the Dharmaguptaka Vinaya School*, beginning with the "Binding of the Precept Area" (sīmābandha);

translated by the Tripiṭaka Master from India, Kang Senghai, during the Cao Wei dynasty. *The Dharmaguptaka Karmavācanās*, one fascicle, beginning with the "Binding of the Great Boundary" (mahāsīmābandha);

translated by the Śramaṇa Tandi from Parthia during the Cao Wei dynasty. *The Dharmaguptaka Bhikṣuṇī Karmavācanā Method*, one fascicle; Dao You states that this is either the *Dharmaguptaka Karmavācanās* or the *Miscellaneous Karmavācanās*, translated during the Song dynasty by [a master] from Kaśmīra.
Translated by Tripiṭaka Guṇavarman. The seven preceding sūtras comprise seven fascicles in one volume, totaling two hundred and two pages.

*Jīshòu Suijí Jiémó* (Abridged and Supplemented *Suijí Karmavācanā* according to the *Dharmaguptaka-vinaya*), one fascicle, compiled by the Śramaṇa Zhìshèng of Chóngfú Monastery, Tang Dynasty. *Sìfēn Sēng Jiémó* (The *Karmavācanā* for the Monks of the Four-Part Vinaya), three fascicles, collected by the Śramaṇa Shì Dàoxuān of Chóngyì Monastery, Tang Dynasty;

titled "Karmavācanā, Fascicle One, Part One," excerpted from the *Dharmaguptaka-vinaya*. *Sìfēn Ní Jiémó* (The *Karmavācanā* for Nuns of the Four-Part Vinaya), three fascicles, collected by the Śramaṇa Shì Huáisù of Xītāiyuán Monastery, Tang Dynasty, based on the Vinaya; titled "Ní Karmavācanā, Fascicle One, Part One," excerpted from the *Dharmaguptaka-vinaya*. These three scriptures, totaling seven fascicles, are contained in the same volume with a combined count of one hundred and eighty-five sheets. [End of Volume] *Rù*.
*Mahāprajāpatī Bhikṣuṇī Sūtra*, two fascicles; also called *Mahāprajāpatī Upasampadā Sūtra* or simply *Mahāprajāpatī Sūtra*. Translator lost;

currently listed by Sengyou as one of the "Different Scriptures from the Liang Region" by Master Dao’an, and is here appended to the Northern Liang catalog. *Kāśyapa-śīla Sūtra*, one fascicle; also called *Mahābhikṣu Sūtra* or simply *Sūtra on the Authentic and False Śramaṇas*.

Translated by the Song layman Juqu Jingsheng. *Sūtra on the Lightness and Heaviness of Retribution for Violating the Precepts*, one fascicle. Extracted from the *Maudgalyāyana-paripṛcchā-vinaya Sūtra*; also called [the Maudgalyāyana...].

*Liánwèn jīng* (Sūtra on Questions and Answers), translated by the Tripiṭaka Master An Shigao of Parthia during the Later Han; one fascicle. Also known as *Jiè xiāozāi jīng* (Sūtra on the Precepts for Eliminating Calamities), translated by the Upāsaka Zhi Qian of Yuezhi during the Wu dynasty;

one fascicle. *Ūpāsaka wǔjièxiàng jīng* (Sūtra on the Characteristics of the Five Precepts for Upāsakas), also titled *Ūpāsaka wǔjiè lüèlùn* (Brief Treatise on the Five Precepts for Upāsakas), translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Guṇavarman of Kaśmīra during the Song dynasty;
one fascicle. *Gēnběn shuōyīqièyǒubù bīnàiyé sòng* (Verses on the Vinaya of the Mūlasarvāstivāda), composed by the Venerable Viśākha; three fascicles.

The *Vinayasūtra* of the Mūlasarvāstivāda School, compiled by the Venerable Jayaprabha; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing during the reign of Empress Wu of the Tang Dynasty. Comprising two fascicles, it totals two hundred and seventy-five sheets. [Mu] [Yi].
The Vinayamātṛkā, ten fascicles, translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Saṃghavarman during the Song dynasty; comprising a total of two hundred and four sheets from one bundle. [All].

The *Vinaya-nidāna-sūtra* (Naiyeyalu), ten fascicles; also known as the *Śīla-nidāna-sūtra*. Translated by the Śramaṇa Zhu Fonian of Liangzhou during the Fu Qin period of the Yao Qin dynasty. A single volume consisting of one hundred and sixty-one sheets. [Gu].

*Śāriputrābhidharma-śāstra* (also known as *Abhidharma-vibhāṣā-śāstra* or simply *Śāriputra-abhidharma*), eighteen fascicles; translated by the foreign śramaṇa Saṃghabhadra during the Xiao Qi dynasty. A single-text edition. *Buddha-abhidharma-sūtra*, two fascicles; also called a *śāstra*; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha of India during the Chen dynasty. The above two scriptures comprise twenty fascicles in two bundles, totaling four hundred and thirty-six sheets. [Bo] [Shu].

The *Vinayamātṛkā-sūtra* in eight fascicles; also called the *Śāstra*, its translator is lost and it is now appended to the Qin records as a single volume. The *Mahābhikṣu-trisahasra-vaipulya-vidhi-sūtra* in two fascicles; also called the *Mahāsāṃghika-vaipulya-vidhi*. Translated by the An-shi Tripiṭaka Master An Shigao of the Later Han. These two aforementioned sūtras comprise ten fascicles in one bundle, totaling two hundred and eight pages. [You].

The *Sarvāstivāda-vinaya-vibhāṣā* in nine fascicles; translator lost, now appended to the *San-Qin-lu*. The single-fascicle text of the *Vinaya-mūla-śāstra-viṃśati-prakaraṇa* (also simply called the *Vimati-cchedikā-śāstra*), translated by the Chen dynasty Tripitaka Master Paramārtha from India. These two scriptures comprise ten fascicles in one volume, totaling two hundred twenty-three sheets. [Zi].

The Abhidharma-piṭaka of the Śrāvakas consists of thirty-six treatises in seventy-two fascicles; these various sections of the Abhidharma-piṭaka differ from one another, and those currently circulating in this region are spoken of here for the sake of the assembly.
Now, based upon the *Mūlasarvāstivāda-śarīra-śāstra* as the primary text,
the *Pādavibhāga-śāstra* occupies the intermediate position,
while the various branches such as the *Vibhāṣā* are arranged at the end.
The other schools being numerous, it is difficult to categorize them systematically;
they shall await future [treatments] without regard for chronological priority.

*Abhidharma-aṣṭagrantha-śāstra*, composed by Kātyāyanīputra; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Saṃghadeva of Kaśmīr, together with Zhu Fonian, during the Fu Qin dynasty. Comprising three bundles, totaling four hundred and seventy-one pages. 【比】【兒】【孔】.

The *Abhidharma-jñānaprasthāna-śāstra*, twenty fascicles, composed by Kātyāyanīputra; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty. The Southern Canon states it is recorded in the *Neidian lu*; comprising two bundles, totaling three hundred and seventy-four pages. [Huái] [ér].

The Abhidharma-dharmaskandha-pāda-śāstra, twelve fascicles, composed by the Venerable Mahakausthila; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang Dynasty. This individual scripture from the Inner Canon comprises one bundle, totaling two hundred and seven sheets. [Fascicle II].

The *Abhidharma-saṃgīti-paryāya-pāda-śāstra*, twenty fascicles, spoken by the Venerable Śāriputra; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang Dynasty. This single work from the *Neidian lu* consists of two bundles, totaling two hundred and eighty-four pages. [Same as above] / [Qi].

The *Prajñapti-pāda-śāstra* consists of eighteen thousand stanzas and was composed by the Venerable Mahākātyāyana. "Kātyāyana" is translated as "Cutter" (翦剃), and "Śunatī" is translated as "Sūnata"; he belonged to a specific class among male Brahmins. This treatise has not yet been translated. The three preceding *Pāda-śāstras* were all composed during the lifetime of the Buddha.

*Abhidharma-vijñānakāya-pāda-śāstra*, sixteen fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang Dynasty; listed as a single work in the *Neidian lu*. *Abhidharma-dhātu-kāya-pāda-śāstra*, three fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang Dynasty. These three treatises above comprise nineteen fascicles and a total of three hundred and thirteen sheets. [Lian] [Zhi].

*Abhidharma-prakaraṇapāda-śāstra*, eighteen fascicles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty. *Saṃgītiparyāya-abhidharma-śāstra*, twelve fascicles. The above two treatises are translations of the same original text with different translations, rendered by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Guṇabhadra together with Buddhabhadra during the Song dynasty. This first set of translations consists of the two aforementioned treatises totaling thirty fascicles in three bundles, comprising four hundred and seventy-nine sheets. [Jiao] [You] [Tou].

The *Abhidharma-vibhāṣā-śāstra*, eighty-two fascicles (or sixty fascicles), translated during the Northern Liang dynasty by Buddhavarman together with Daotai. From the eighth bundle, totaling one thousand four hundred and four sheets. [Fen] [Qie] [Mo] [Zhen] [Gui] [Ren] [Ci] [Yin].

The *Abhidharma-mahāvibhāṣā-śāstra*, two hundred fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang Dynasty; comprising twenty bundles, totaling three thousand one hundred and sixty-eight sheets. The Abhidharmakośa-bhāṣya, thirty fascicles, composed by the Venerable Vasubandhu; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang Dynasty. Recorded in the Neidian lu. Second translation: three bundles, totaling four hundred and seventy-nine sheets. [Zhen] [Zhi] [Man].

The Abhidharma-nyāyānusāra-śāstra, eighty fascicles, composed by the Venerable Saṅghabhadra; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang Dynasty. Recorded in the fourth volume of the *Neidian lu* as a single work, comprising eight bundles and totaling one thousand four hundred twenty-three sheets. [Character-by-character gloss]: Pursuit, things, intention, shifting, firmness, upholding, noble conduct.

The Abhidharmasamaya-nirdeśa-śāstra, forty fascicles, composed by the Venerable Saṅghabhadra; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang Dynasty. Composed by the Mahābhadanta Upaśānta; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Narendrayaśas of India in conjunction with Fazhi during the Northern Qi dynasty. These two treatises comprise ten fascicles in a single volume, totaling one hundred eighty-one pages. [Total].

*Saṃyuktābhidharmahṛdaya-śāstra*, eleven fascicles; also known as *Saṃyuktābhidharma-vibhāṣā*. Composed by the Venerable Dharmatrāta. Composed by the Venerable Ghoṣaka. Translated during the Cao Wei period; the name of the Tripiṭaka Master is lost. *Lakṣaṇānusāra-śāstra*, two fascicles; alternatively titled *Guṇamati-lakṣaṇānusāra-śāstra*. Composed by Dharma Master Guṇamati. Translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha during the Chen dynasty. The above three treatises comprise fifteen fascicles in two bundles, totaling three hundred and seventy-two sheets. [Yi] [Hua].

*The Treatise Compiled by the Venerable Vasumitra Bodhisattva*, ten fascicles; composed by the Venerable Vasumitra; translated by the Kapiśa Tripiṭaka Master Saṃghabhūti and others of the Fu Qin dynasty. *The Tridharmaka-śāstra*, three fascicles (alternatively called a *sūtra* or in two fascicles); translated by the Kapiśa Tripiṭaka Master Gautama Saṃghadeva of the Eastern Jin dynasty. *The Abhidharma-avatāra-śāstra*, two fascicles; composed by the Arhat Skandhila; translated by the Tang Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang. *Lokasthāna-abhidharma-śāstra* (Treatise on the Establishment of the World), ten fascicles; alternatively titled *Lun* (Treatise). Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha of Central India during the Chen dynasty. This single volume comprises one hundred and seventy sheets. [Beijing Edition].
*Vimuktimārga-śāstra*, twelve fascicles, translated by the Tripitaka Master Saṃghavarman of Funan during the Liang Dynasty; from one bundle, totaling one hundred and one sheets. [Back].
