According to the *Fanjing tu* (Catalogue of Translated Scriptures), these two treatises comprise twenty-five fascicles, totaling four hundred and seventy-eight sheets across two volumes. [Máng] [Miàn].

The *Vibhāṣā-śāstra* (鞞婆沙論), fourteen fascicles, also titled the *Vibhāṣā-abhidharma-śāstra*, composed by the Arhat Śītapāṇi; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Saṃghabhūti of Kapiśa during the Fu Qin dynasty. The *Sammitīya-nikāya-śāstra* (三彌底部論), three fascicles—or four fascicles without the character "bu" (部); *Sammitī* means "Right Measure" (正量) in Chinese, referring to a treatise within the Sammitīya school. Translator unknown; currently appended to the Fu Qin records. The two aforementioned treatises comprise seventeen fascicles in two bundles, totaling three hundred and eighty-five sheets. [Luo] [Fu].

*Vibhāṣā-śāstra* (Treatise on the Analysis of Merit), three fascicles; alternatively said to be a lost translation, included in the Later Han catalogue. *Catur-ārya-satya-śāstra* (Treatise on the Four Noble Truths), four fascicles; composed by Vasubhadra; translated by the Chen dynasty Indian Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha. *Pratyekabuddha-nidāna-śāstra* (Treatise on the Causes and Conditions of Pratyekabuddhas), one fascicle or two fascicles; lost translation, now appended to the Qin catalogue. *Aṣṭādaśa-nikāya-śāstra* (Treatise on the Eighteen Schools), one fascicle; newly classified as a lost translation, appended to the Three Qin catalogues. *Nikāyabheda-vibhaṅga-śāstra* (Treatise on the Differences in Sectarian Tenets), one fascicle; also titled *Nikāya-bheda-śāstra*; translated by the Chen dynasty Indian Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha. *Nikāyabhedopadeśa-saṃgraha-śāstra* (Treatise on the Wheel of the Different Sectarian Doctrines), one fascicle; composed by the Bodhisattva Vasumitra; translated by the Tang dynasty Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang. [Recorded in] the *Fanying tu* (Illustrated Catalogue of Translated Scriptures), Volume Upper: these six treatises total eleven fascicles, contained in one bundle, comprising one hundred and ninety-seven sheets. [Wei].

The *Biographies of Sages and Worthies* (Shengxian zhuan) consists of seven bundles; the collection of translated biographies from Sanskrit originals comprises sixty-eight works in one hundred and seventy-three fascicles. The *Buddhacarita-kāvya* (Fo suoxing zan jing zhuan), also known as the *Buddha-pūrvacaryā-sūtra* (Fobenxing jing), in five fascicles, was composed by the Bodhisattva Aśvaghoṣa and translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmakṣema of India during the Northern Liang dynasty. The *Buddha-pūrvacaryā-sūtra* (Fobenxing jing), in one fascicle, also titled the *Buddha-pūrvacaryā-praśaṃsā-avadāna* (Fobenxing zan zhuan), was translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Baoyun of Liangzhou during the Song dynasty. These two collections total twelve fascicles in the same bundle, comprising two hundred and fifteen sheets. [Based on].

*Zhuanjibaiyuan jing* (The Sutra of One Hundred Compiled Avenues), ten fascicles, translated by the Yuezhi upāsaka Zhi Qian of the Wu dynasty; according to the *Neidian lu*, it comprises one bundle totaling one hundred fifty-two sheets. [Jing]

The *Chuyao jing* (Sūtra of the Exalted Sayings), twenty fascicles; also known as the *Lun*. Translated during the Fu Qin period by the Śramaṇa Zhu Fonian of Liangzhou. The *Xianyu jing* (Sūtra of the Wise and the Foolish), thirteen fascicles—according to the *Fanying tu* (Diagram of Translated Scriptures), it is also recorded as fifteen, six, or ten fascicles. Translated by the Śramaṇas Huijue and others of Liangzhou during the Yuan Wei dynasty at Gaochang Commandery. These two aforementioned scriptures comprise thirty-three fascicles in four bundles, totaling seven hundred and ninety-seven sheets. [Palaces and towers] rise in dense profusion.

*Daodi jing* (Sūtra on the Stages of the Path), one fascicle; sometimes the character "da" (great) is added. An excerpt from the *Xiuxing jing* (Sūtra on Practice); originally a brief foreign version, translated by the Anxi Tripiṭaka Master An Shigao of the Later Han. *Xiuxing daodi jing* (Sūtra on the Stages of the Path of Practice), seven fascicles; also called the *Xiuxing jing*. Translated by the Western Jin Tripiṭaka Master Zhu Fahu. Third translation; one of the three translations is missing. *Sengqialuocha suoji jing* (Saṃgharakṣa’s Saṃyukta-saṃgraha Sūtra), five fascicles, compiled by Saṃgharakṣa; translated by the Fu Qin Tripiṭaka Master Saṃghabhūti and others. The above three collections comprise fourteen fascicles in a single volume, totaling two hundred thirty-one sheets. [Liu].

*The Sūtra of One Hundred Parables*, two fascicles, compiled by Saṃghasena; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Guṇabhadra of India during the Qi dynasty of the Xiao family. *The Sūtra of the Original Causes of the Bodhisattvas*, four fascicles, compiled by Saṃghasena; translated by the lay devotee Zhi Qian of Yuezhi during the Wu dynasty. *The Essential Compendium of Various Mahāyāna Sūtras on the Gate of Bodhisattva Practice*, three fascicles, translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Zhiyan of Zhixiang Temple during the Tang dynasty. These three collections comprise nine fascicles in one volume, totaling one hundred and ninety-one sheets. [Guan].

*The Transmission of the Dharma-treasury through Successive Causes and Conditions*, six fascicles; alternatively titled *Without the Words "Causes and Conditions"*. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kiṅkiaya of the Western Regions in collaboration with Tanyao during the Northern Wei dynasty.

*The Sūtra on the Samādhi of Seated Meditation*, two fascicles; also known as the *Sūtra on the Bodhisattva’s Methods of Meditation* or simply the *Meditation Sūtra*. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty. *The Sūtra of the Buddha-Physician*, one fascicle; also called the *Sūtra of the Buddha-Physician King*.

Translated by the Indian Śramaṇa Zhú Lùyán in collaboration with Zhī Yuè during the Wu dynasty. *The Sūtra of Various Difficulties Regarding the Sole Sun*, one fascicle. Translated by the Yuezhi Upāsaka Zhī [Fàng] of the Wu dynasty.
*The Sūtra on Mahākāśyapa’s Journey to the Buddha’s Parinirvāṇa*, translated by Qian; also known as *The Sūtra on Kāśyapa’s Journey to the Buddha’s Nirvāṇa*.

Translated by the Western Region Śramaṇa Zhu Fatai and Dharmaruci during the Eastern Jin dynasty. *The Sūtra on the Bodhisattva’s Condemnation of Lust*, one fascicle; also known as [simply] *The Sūtra*. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty. *The Sūtra on the Fourfold Training*, one fascicle; sometimes the word "Sūtra" is omitted.
Translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Guṇabhadra of the Song dynasty. *The Sūtra on the Secret Traces Vajra-wielder’s Lamentation upon the Buddha’s Entry into Nirvāṇa*.

*Sūtra on the Verses on the Extinction of the Dharma Spoken by Kātyāyana*, one fascicle; translator lost, now appended to the Qin records. *Sūtra on the Verses on the Extinction of the Dharma Spoken by Kātyāyana*, one fascicle; Sengyou’s record states it was a lost translation by Master Dao’an;

now appended to the Xiqin records. *Sūtra on the Buddha Healing the Body*, one fascicle; alternatively titled *Sūtra on Healing the Body*; Sengyou’s record states it was a lost translation by Master Dao’an;

now appended to the Western Jin records. *Sūtra on Governing the Mind*, one fascicle; alternatively titled *Sūtra on the Buddha Governing the Mind*; Sengyou’s record states it was a lost translation by Master Dao’an; now appended to the Western Jin records. The above eleven collections comprise seventeen fascicles in total.
One fascicle comprising one hundred and seventy-two sheets:

the *Zá bǎozàng jīng* (Sutra of the Storehouse of Miscellaneous Jewels), eight fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kikkaya of the Western Regions during the Northern Wei, together with Tanyao; the *Nàxiān bǐqiū jīng* (Sutra of the Bhikṣu Nāgasena), three fascicles—or two fascicles—or simply titled the *Nàxiān jīng*, of lost translation, appended to the Eastern Jin records. The above two collections comprise eleven fascicles in one fascicle, totaling one hundred and eighty-nine sheets. [Jing].
*The Essential Sūtra on the Five-Gate Dhyāna* (Wǔmén chán yào yòng jīng), one fascicle;

composed by the Great Dhyāna Master Buddhamitra and translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmamitra of Kaśmīra during the Song dynasty. *The Dhyāna Sūtra of Dharmatrāta* (Dá mó duō luó chán jīng), two fascicles; also titled *The Dhyāna Sūtra of the Contemplation of Impurity* (Bùjìng guān chán jīng); [containing] the "Expedient Means for Practice" (*Xiūxíng fāngbiàn*).

Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin dynasty. *The Essential Explanation of the Dhyāna Method* (Chánfǎ yàojiě), two fascicles; also titled *The Essential Sūtra of Dhyāna* (Chányào jīng). Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty.

*Chanyao heyu jing* (Sutra on the Essentials of Dhyāna: Rebuking Desire), one fascicle; titled *Chanyao jing, Heyu pin* (Sutra on the Essentials of Dhyāna, Chapter on Rebuking Desire); translated during the Later Han, translator lost. *Neshen guan zhangju jing* (Sutra on the Contemplation of the Internal Body in Chapters and Phrases), one fascicle; translated during the Later Han, translator lost. *Faguang jing* (Sutra on the Contemplation of Dharmas), one fascicle;

translated by the Western Jin Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa. *Siliyao fa* (The Essential Methods of Contemplation), one fascicle; alternatively titled with the word "sūtra" (*jing*) added; translated by the Yao Qin Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva.

*Shieryou jing* (Sutra on the Twelve Wanderings), one fascicle; translated by the Śramaṇa Kālodaka from the Western Regions during the Eastern Jin. *Jiu za piyu jing* (Old Sutra of Miscellaneous Parables), two fascicles; likewise [translated during the Later Han, translator lost].
*The Scripture of Miscellaneous Parables* (*Zā pìyù jí jīng*), translated by the Tripitaka Master Kang Senghui of India during the Wu dynasty; one fascicle.

*The Scripture of Miscellaneous Parables* (*Zā pìyù jīng*), translated by the Tripitaka Master Zhi Loujiachen of Yuezhi during the Later Han dynasty; one fascicle. The above ten collections comprise thirteen fascicles in one volume, totaling one hundred and ninety-one sheets.

*The Scripture of Miscellaneous Parables* (*Zā pìyù jīng*), two fascicles, also titled *The Scripture on the Bodhisattva Saving Sentient Beings* (*Púsà dù rén jīng*); translator lost, included in the records of the Later Han. *The Scripture of Miscellaneous Parables* (*Zā pìyù jīng*), two fascicles, compiled by the Bhikṣu Daoli; translated by the Tripitaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty. *The Scripture of Parables of King Aśoka* (*Āyù wáng pìyù jīng*), one fascicle; translator lost, appended to the records of the Eastern Jin. *The Scripture of King Aśoka* (*Āyù wáng jīng*), ten fascicles (sometimes with the character "Da" [Great] prefixed); translated by the Tripitaka Master Saṃghavarman of Funan during the Liang dynasty. The above four collections comprise fifteen fascicles in one volume, totaling one hundred and eighty-six sheets. [Copy].

*The Biography of King Aśoka*, five fascicles (alternatively seven fascicles), also titled *The Mahā-aśokarāja-sūtra*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master An Fashen of Parthia during the Western Jin dynasty. *The Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of King Aśoka’s Son Losing His Eyesight*, two fascicles; also known as *The Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of Prince Dharmavardhana Losing His Eyesight*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmanandi of India during the Yao Qin dynasty under the Fu Qin regime. *An Abstract Explanation of the Four Āgamas*, two fascicles, compiled by the Arhat Vasubhadra and translated by the Kuchean Śramaṇa Kumārabuddhi and others under the Fu Qin regime. The above three collections comprise nine fascicles in one volume, totaling one hundred and seventy sheets. [Qin] *** **Note:** The term "禽" (*qín*) at the end of the entry is a traditional cataloging mark used in the *Taishō Shinshū Daizōkyō* to indicate the section of the canon where the text is classified (in this case, the "Bird" or *Qin* section). It has been omitted from the translation as it is not part of the bibliographic description of the text itself.

*The Dhammapada Sūtra*, two fascicles; also known as *The Collection of the Dhammapada*, compiled by the Venerable Dharmatrāta and translated by the Indian śramaṇa Vighnanandin and others of the Wu [Dynasty].
*The Dhammapada-avadāna Sūtra*, four fascicles; also titled *The Sūtra on the Origins and Conclusions of the Dhammapada*, translated by the śramaṇas Śikṣānanda and Fali of the Western Jin.

*Kāśyapa-paripṛcchā Sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by An Shigao, the Tripiṭaka Master of Parthia during the Later Han. *The Transmission of the Compiled Tripiṭaka and Miscellaneous Piṭakas*, one fascicle.

*Sanhui jing* (Sūtra on the Three Wisdoms), one fascicle; translator lost, now appended to the Eastern Jin catalogue. Sengyou’s catalogue states it was a "different sūtra" by Master Dao’an; now appended to the Northern Liang catalogue. *Abidamo wufa xing jing* (Abhidharma-sūtra on the Five Dharmas), one fascicle;

also simply titled *Abidamo* or *Kuhui* (Bitter Wisdom); sometimes the characters "xing" (practice) or "er" (two) are omitted. Translated by An Shigao, Tripiṭaka Master from Parthia, during the Later Han.

*Ahan koujie shier yinyuan jing* (Āgama Sūtra on the Oral Explanation of the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination), one fascicle; also simply called the *Ahan koujie jing*, or named the *Duan shier yinyuan jing* (Sūtra on Severing the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination). Translated by the Upāsaka from Parthia during the Later Han.
*The Sūtra on the Stages of the Minor Path* (Xiaodao di jing), one fascicle, translated by the Western Regions Tripiṭaka Master Zhi Yao of the Later Han;

*The Mañjuśrī’s Vow Sūtra* (Wenshushili fayuan jing), one fascicle—alternatively titled *Mañjuśrī’s Vow Gāthās*—translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Buddhabhadra of the Eastern Jin; *The Names of Six Bodhisattvas*, one fascicle—the *Chángfáng Rùzàng Lù* states that the *Names of Six Bodhisattvas* should also be recited and maintained;
*One Hundred and Fifty Verses in Praise of the Buddha*, one fascicle, composed by the Venerable Mātṛceṭa; translated during the Later Han with the translator lost.

*The Collection of the Rākṣasa of Ignorance* (one fascicle), also titled *The Scripture of the Rākṣasa of Ignorance* (alternatively two fascicles); translator lost, now appended to the Qin records. *The Biography of Bodhisattva Aśvaghoṣa* (one fascicle); translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin. *The Biography of Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna* (one fascicle); translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin. *The Biography of Bodhisattva Āryadeva* (one fascicle); translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin. *The Biography of Dharma Master Vasubandhu* (one fascicle); translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha of Central India during the Chen dynasty. *A Verse Summary of the Essential Teachings Spoken by Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna for King Śāntaka* (one fascicle); translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Guṇavarman of Kaśmīra during the Song dynasty; listed in the old Tang catalogs. *A Verse Summary for Encouraging Kings* (one fascicle); composed by Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna.

*The Sūtra of the Verses of Advice to the King by Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Saṃghavarman of India during the Song Dynasty; one fascicle. *The Sūtra on Piṇḍola Bharadvāja Preaching the Dharma for King Udayana*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing of the Tang Dynasty; one fascicle. Also titled *The Sūtra on Piṇḍola Preaching the Dharma for the King*.

*The Sūtra on the Great Hero Bodhisattva’s Brief Exposition of Karmic Retribution*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Guṇabhadra of India during the Song Dynasty; contained within this fascicle. *The Method for Inviting Piṇḍola*, one fascicle (or with the word "sūtra" added). Translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Huìjiǎn of the Song Dynasty. *The Brief Exposition of Karmic Retribution*, one fascicle. Composed by the Great Hero Bodhisattva (or with the word "collection" added).

*The Scripture on the Transformations of the Future Spoken by Bhikṣu Kātyāyanīputra*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Saṃghavarman of India during the Song dynasty, one fascicle. This was originally a scripture of lost translation in Sengyou’s catalogue; it is now appended to the Song record. *The Record of the Persistence of the Dharma Spoken by the Great Arhat Nandimitra*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty, one fascicle. *Sāṃkhyakārikā* (The Seventy Verses on Gold), also known as the *Sāṃkhya-śāstra*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha of India during the Chen dynasty, three fascicles. *Daśapadārthī* (The Ten Categories of the Victorious School), translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty, one fascicle. The above fifteen works comprise eighteen fascicles in a single volume, totaling two hundred and twenty sheets. [Painting]

This collection of works composed in this region comprises forty treatises in three hundred and sixty-eight fascicles: *The Genealogy of Śākyamuni* (Śākyapuṭa), ten fascicles; differing from the current version in its breadth and brevity. Compiled by the *śramaṇa* Sengyou of Jianchu Monastery during the Qi dynasty. *A Brief Genealogy of the Śākya Clan*, one fascicle; sometimes lacking the character "brief" (*lue*). Compiled by the *śramaṇa* Shi Daoxuan of Ximing Monastery during the Tang dynasty. *The Topography of Śākyamuni* (Śākyafangzhi), two fascicles. Compiled by the *śramaṇa* Shi Daoxuan of Ximing Monastery during the Tang dynasty. The above three collections comprise thirteen fascicles in two volumes, totaling three hundred and seventy-six sheets. [Characters: 綵 (cai) and 仙 (xian)].

*Jīnglǜ yìxiàng* (Diverse Features of Sūtras and Vinaya), fifty fascicles. Compiled by order of Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty in the fifteenth year of the Tiānjiàn era by the śramaṇa Bǎochàng and others. Comprising five bundles, totaling eight hundred and fifty-four sheets. [Líng] [Bǐng] [Shè] [Báng] [Qǐ].
The *Dhāraṇī-saṃgraha* in ten fascicles; the author is unknown. It is now appended to the Liang dynasty catalog. Comprising one bundle, it totals two hundred and seventy-one sheets. [Section A].

The Compendium of Essential Passages from Various Sutras, twenty fascicles, translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Xuanyun of Ximing Monastery during the Tang Dynasty; totaling five hundred and ninety sheets across three bundles. [Zhang] [Dui] [Ying].

The *Chusanzangjiji* (Collection for the Compilation of Records Concerning the Tripitaka), fifteen fascicles, compiled by the Śramaṇa Shi Sengyou of Jianchu Monastery during the Liang dynasty; and the *Zhongjing mulu* (Catalogue of All Scriptures), seven fascicles, compiled by the Śramaṇas Fa-jing and others by imperial decree in the fourteenth year of the Kaihuang era. The aforementioned two collections comprise twenty-two fascicles in two bundles, totaling four hundred and thirty-four sheets. [肆] [筵].

The *Kaihuang Sanbao Lu* (Record of the Three Jewels of the Kaihuang Era), fifteen fascicles; its internal title states: *Lidai Sanbao Ji* (Chronicle of the Three Jewels through Successive Dynasties), compiled by Fei Changfang of Chengdu, a scholar-translator during the seventeenth year of the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty. The *Zhongjing Mulü* (Catalogue of All Scriptures), five fascicles, compiled by imperial decree in the second year of the Renshou era of the Sui dynasty for the śramaṇas and scholars engaged in translation. These two collections comprise twenty fascicles in two bundles, totaling three hundred and fifty-three sheets. [She] [Xi].

The Record of the Inner Scriptures of the Great Tang, ten fascicles, compiled by the Śramaṇa Shi Daoxuan of Ximing Monastery during the Tang Dynasty; comprising one bundle, totaling two hundred and ninety-five sheets. [Gǔ]

*Continuation of the Catalogue of the Inner Scriptures of the Great Tang*, one fascicle, compiled by the Śramaṇa Shi Zhi-sheng of Xichongfu Monastery during the Tang dynasty; *Illustrated Record of Translations of Scriptures from Antiquity to the Present*, four fascicles, compiled by the Śramaṇa Shi Jing-mai, a Translator of Scriptures during the Tang dynasty; *Continuation of the Illustrated Record of Translations of Scriptures from Antiquity to the Present*, one fascicle, compiled by the Śramaṇa Shi Zhi-sheng of Xichongfu Monastery during the Tang dynasty; *Great Weekly Catalogue for the Collation and Determination of All Scriptures*, fifteen fascicles, compiled by order of Empress Wu of the Tang dynasty by the Śramaṇa Ming-quan and others of Foshouji Monastery. These four collections comprise twenty-one fascicles in two bundles, totaling three hundred and fifty sheets. [瑟] [吹].

The Kaiyuan Catalogue of Buddhist Teachings, twenty fascicles, compiled by the Śramaṇa Shi Zhisheng of Xichongfu Monastery during the Tang Dynasty; comprising two bundles, totaling five hundred eighty-one sheets. [Sheng] [Sheng].

*Yiqiejing yinyi* (Phonetics and Meanings of All Scriptures), twenty-five fascicles, compiled by the Tang dynasty Śramaṇa Xuanying; recorded in the *Neidian lu*. *Xinyi Dafangguang Fo Huayanjing yinyi* (Phonetics and Meanings of the Newly Translated Avataṃsaka Sūtra), two fascicles, compiled by the Tang dynasty Śramaṇa Huiyuan of Jingfasi Temple. The above two collections comprise twenty-seven fascicles in four bundles, totaling five hundred and forty-one pages. [Characters: 階 (jiē), 納 (nà), 陛 (bì), 弁 (biàn)].

*The Great Tang Records on the Western Regions*, twelve fascicles, compiled by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang; recorded in the *Neidian lu*. *Collected Evaluations of Buddhist and Daoist Debates from Antiquity to the Present*, four fascicles, compiled by the Śramaṇa Shi Daoxuan of Ximing Monastery of the Tang; recorded in the *Neidian lu*. *Continued Collection of Evaluations of Buddhist and Daoist Debates from Antiquity to the Present*, one fascicle, compiled by the Śramaṇa Shi Zhisheng of Chongfu Monastery of the Tang. The above three collections comprise sixteen fascicles in two volumes, totaling three hundred and forty-two sheets. [Categorized as] "Translated" or "Doubtful."

*The Record of the Miraculous Responses of the Triple Gem in the Eastern Lands*, three fascicles; from the *Neidian lu* (Catalogue of Buddhist Scriptures), compiled by the Śramaṇa Shi Daoxuan of Ximing Monastery during the Tang dynasty. *The Collected Rites for Śramaṇas Not Bowing to the Laity*, six fascicles; from the *Neidian lu*, compiled by the Śramaṇa Yancong of Hongfu Monastery during the Tang dynasty. These two collections comprise nine fascicles in one volume, totaling two hundred and one pages. [Xing]

The Biography of the Tripitaka Master of Great Ci’en Monastery, ten fascicles, compiled by the Śramaṇa Huili of Xitaiyuan Monastery during the Tang Dynasty; comprising one bundle, totaling one hundred and ninety-three sheets. [Right].

*Biographies of Eminent Monks Who Sought the Dharma in the Western Regions of the Great Tang*, two fascicles; compiled by the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing of the Tang. *The Biography of Faxian*, one fascicle; also titled *A Record of Travels through India*. Recorded by the Śramaṇa Faxian of the Eastern Jin Dynasty concerning his own travels to India; included in the *Changfang Lu*. *Biographies of Eminent Monks*, fourteen fascicles; one fascicle is a catalog; included in the *Changfang Lu*. Compiled by the Śramaṇa Huijiao of Jiaxiang Temple in Kuaiji during the Liang Dynasty. The above three collections comprise seventeen fascicles in two bundles, totaling three hundred eighty-one sheets. [Tong] [Guang].

The *Continued Biographies of Eminent Monks* (Xu gaoseng zhuan), thirty-one fascicles, is recorded in the *Neidian lu* (Catalogue of Buddhist Scriptures). Compiled by the Śramaṇa Shi Daoxuan of Ximing Monastery during the Tang Dynasty, the aforementioned thirty-one fascicles are divided into four bundles (zhì), totaling seven hundred and ninety-two pages. [Contents: Nei, Zuo, Da, Cheng.]

*Biànzhènglùn* (Discourse on the Rectification of Orthodoxy), eight fascicles; listed in the *Neidiànlù*. Compiled by the Śramaṇa Fālín of Longnánshān Lóngtián Temple during the Táng dynasty. Listed in the *Neidiànlù*, Upper Collection, eight fascicles in one volume, totaling one hundred eighty-four pages. [Ming].

*Poxie lun* (Treatise on Destroying Heresies), two fascicles; compiled by the Śramaṇa Falin of Longnan Mountain Longtian Temple during the Tang dynasty. *Zhengzhen lun* (Treatise on Distinguishing the Correct), three fascicles; compiled by the Śramaṇa Xuanyi of Foshouji Temple during the era of Empress Wu of the Tang dynasty. *Shimen bianhuo lun* (Treatise on Discerning Delusions in Ten Sections), two fascicles; compiled by the Śramaṇa Fuli of Xingshan Temple during the Tang dynasty. *Hongming ji* (Collection for Propagating and Clarifying [the Faith]), fourteen fascicles; compiled by the Śramaṇa Sengyou of Jianchu Temple during the Liang dynasty. These four collections comprise twenty-one fascicles in two bundles, totaling two hundred seventy-one sheets. [Ji] [Ji] [Fen].

*Guang hongming ji* (The Collection for the Wide Propagation and Clarification of the Orthodox Teaching), thirty fascicles, compiled by the monk Daoxuan of Ximing Monastery during the Tang Dynasty; recorded in the *Changfang lu*. The first collection consists of thirty-seven fascicles, divided into three bundles, totaling one thousand and two sheets. [Dian] [Yi] [Ju].

*Jí zhū jīng lǐchàn yí* (Ritual for Repentance and Prostration According to Various Scriptures), two fascicles; compiled by Śramaṇa Zhisheng of Xichongfu Monastery during the Tang Dynasty. *Dàtáng nánhǎi jìguī nèifǎ zhuàn* (Record of the Inner Dharma Sent Back from the South Seas of the Great Tang), four fascicles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing of the Tang Dynasty. *Bǐqiūní zhuàn* (Biographies of Bhikṣuṇīs), four fascicles; compiled by Śramaṇa Baoshang of Zhuangyan Monastery during the Liang Dynasty. *Biéshuō zuìyào xíngfǎ* (Essential Methods for the Practice of Confessing Sins), one fascicle; sometimes without the character "bié"; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing of the Tang Dynasty. *Shòuyòng sānshuǐ yào fǎ* (Essential Methods for the Three Waters for Use), one fascicle; also titled *Yàoxíngfǎ*; compiled by the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing of the Tang Dynasty. *Hùmìng fāngshēng guǐyí* (Ritual for Saving Life and Releasing Creatures), one fascicle; also titled *Guǐyífǎ*; compiled by the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing of the Tang Dynasty. The above six works comprise thirteen fascicles in one bundle, totaling two hundred and three pages. [Qun].

The *Kaiyuan Shijiao Lu* (Record of Buddhist Teachings Compiled during the Kaiyuan Era), four fascicles, compiled by the śramaṇa Zhisheng of Xichongfu Monastery in the Tang dynasty; and the *Kaiyuan Shijiao Lu Bielu* (Supplementary Record of the Kaiyuan Shijiao Lu): the *Han Faba Neizhuan* (Inner Biography of the Dharma Origin in China), five fascicles, whose author is unknown; and the *Śramaṇa Falin Biezhuàn* (Separate Biography of the Śramaṇa Falin), three fascicles, compiled by the śramaṇa Yanzong. Regarding these two latter works, because they were clearly prohibited by imperial decree and not permitted to circulate, they are not included in this compilation; nevertheless, they have been copied and transmitted from generation to generation.
Not included in the Tripitaka, etc., according to the *Kaiyuan Shijiao Lu*, Volume 20, End: *Ji ji jin gang li shi jing* (Sutra on the Traces Left by the Vajrapāṇi), seven fascicles;

*Bodhisattva meng jing* (Sutra of the Bodhisattva’s Dream), two fascicles; *Ren jing tian zi hui fa jie ti xing wu fen bie jing* (Sutra on the Assembly of the Sons of the Pure Abode Gods Concerning the Non-differentiation of the Essential Nature of the Dharmadhātu), two fascicles—renamed *Daji* (Mahāsaṃnipāta);
*Shi fa jing* (Sutra of the Ten Dharmas), one fascicle—added to the name *Daji*.
*Daśadharmaka-sūtra*, twenty fascicles; *Buddhabhāṣita-nanda-nirvāṇa-garbha-praveśa-sūtra*, two fascicles;
*Mañjuśrī-vyākaraṇa-sūtra*, three fascicles; *Bodhisattva-dṛṣṭatattva-samādhi-sūtra*, sixteen fascicles;
*Bodhisattva-piṭaka-sūtra*, three fascicles (renamed the *Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra-parivarta*); *Rāṣṭrapāla-bodhisattva-sūtra*, three fascicles.
*The Sūtra of the Questions of the Householder Ugga*, one fascicle; *The Kāśyapa Sūtra*, two fascicles; *The Sūtra of the Questions of the Bodhisattva Mahākāśyapa*, one fascicle;
*The Sūtra of the Questions of the Bodhisattva Subāhu*, two fascicles; *The Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Vimaladattā’s Analysis of Responsive Eloquence*, one fascicle;
*The Sūtra of the Girl Abhayamati*, one fascicle; and *The Mahāvaipulya Sūtra of the Questions of the Devaputra Susthitamati*, four fascicles.
The *Mahāyānopāya-sūtra*, three fascicles; the *Vijñānasaṃkrānti-sūtra*, two fascicles, renamed the *Saddharma-kulaputra-parivarta*;
the *Maitreya-bodhisattva-paripṛcchā-sūtra*, one fascicle, renamed the *Maitreya-aṣṭadharma-parivarta*;
the *Mahāratnakūṭa-sūtra*, one fascicle, renamed the *Samantaprabha-bodhisattva-parivarta*; the *Ratnarāśi-sūtra*, two fascicles; and the *Ratnaśikhara-bodhisattva-paripṛcchā*.
The two fascicles [of the *Dharmarakṣa-sūtra*] and the twenty-two sections of the *Guhyapāda-malla-sūtra*, totaling eighty fascicles, have all been incorporated into the *Mahāratnakūṭa-sūtra-piṭaka*;
therefore, no separate editions exist.

The *New Sūtra on the Practice of the Way* (Xīndàoxíngjīng), seven fascicles: having examined the various versions held in the collections, all are identical in text to the *Shorter Version* (*Xiǎopǐn*), differing only in their titles; therefore, I have not transcribed it separately. As for the *Practice of the Way*, I have searched for it but could not find it. The *Mahāvaipulya Mahāsaṃnipāta Sūtra*, eight fascicles: this is the combined sixth bundle of the *Mahāsaṃnipāta Sūtra*; it is currently present in a separate edition.
The first fascicle is the *Bore wushi jiaojì jīng* (Sūtra of the Fifty Evaluations of the Perfection of Wisdom).

The subsequent six fascicles consist of two fascicles of the *Wújìn yì ānòudá lóngwáng jīng* (Sūtra of the Dragon King Anavatapta of Infinite Intent), which are identical in their entirety to the *Hóngdào guǎngxiǎn sānmèi jīng* (Sūtra on the Samādhi of Extensively Manifesting the Broad Way) found in the canon; and three fascicles of the *Hé dào shénzú jīng* (Sūtra of the Divine Footsteps that Unite the Way).

The *Yùzàng Zhōngdào Shénzú Wújí Biànhuà* (The Infinite Transformations of the Divine Footsteps of the Middle Way within the Treasury) is identical in its textual phrasing to the three-fascicle *Āiqì Jīng* (Sutra of Lamentation).
The *Fāngděng Pānnièpán* (Vaipulya Parinirvāṇa) is identical in its textual phrasing to the version in the canon.

The one-fascicle *Bǎosī Huìyìn Sānmèi Jīng* (Treasure-Thought Wisdom-Seal Samādhi Sutra) is identical in its textual phrasing to the *Huìyìn Sānmèi* (Wisdom-Seal Samādhi) in the canon. The one-fascicle *Lùzǐ Jīng* (Śarabha Sutra) [is likewise].
The *Mṛgajā-sūtra* (鹿母經) is identical in wording to the version in the Tibetan Canon;
the *Sukhāvatīvyūha-sūtra* (小無量壽經), one fascicle, is identical in wording to the *Amitābha-sūtra* (阿彌陀經) in the Tibetan Canon;

the *Garbhakośa-sūtra* (胎藏經), one fascicle, is identical in wording to the *Vimaladattā-sūtra* (無垢質女經) in the Tibetan Canon; and the *Śrāvastī-dvādaśāṅga-pratītyasamutpāda-sūtra* (聞城十二因緣經), one fascicle.
The *Sūtra on Contemplating the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination* is identical in its wording to the *Baiṭuśāpao jīng* (Pāṭaliputra Sūtra) found in the Tripiṭaka;
the one-fascicle *Dà ānbān jīng* (Great Ānāpāna Sūtra) is identical in its entirety to the first fascicle of the *Dà ānbān shǒuyì jīng* (Great Ānāpāna-śmṛti Sūtra) found in the Tripiṭaka;

the one-fascicle *Shēnrì jīng* (Śreṇika Sūtra) is identical in its wording to the *Yuèguāng tóngzǐ jīng* (Candraprabha-kumāra Sūtra) found in the Tripiṭaka; and the one-fascicle *Zhuǎnlún wǔdào zuìfú bàoyìng jīng* (Sūtra on the Retribution of Sin and Merit in the Five Realms of the Wheel of Saṃsāra).
The *Zhēngzhàng zhōng zuìfú bàoyìng jīng* (Sūtra on the Retribution of Offenses and Merits in the Treasury) is identical in its textual content to the [corresponding] sūtra in the Canon.
The *Zhāntuóyuè jīng* (Cāṇḍālaya Sūtra), one fascicle, is identical in both wording and phrasing to the *Zhāntuóyuè guówáng jīng* (Sūtra of King Cāṇḍālaya) in the Canon.

The *Zhēnwěi shā mén jīng* (Sūtra of Authentic and Spurious Śramaṇas), one fascicle, is identical in wording and phrasing to the *Jiāshè jìn jīng* (Kāśyapa Prohibition Sūtra) in the Canon. The *Zhuǎnfǎlún jīng* (Sūtra of Turning the Wheel of Dharma), one fascicle.

Upon examining the versions found within the various Tripitaka collections, they are all sūtras concerning the Turning of the Wheel of Dharma (*Dharmacakra-pravartana*). The *Dharmacakra-pravartana-sūtra* is identical in its entirety to this [text].
The one-fascicle *Piṇḍola-bhāradvāja-dharma-deśanā-rāja-sūtra* is identical in its wording to the version in the canon concerning Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja preaching the Dharma to King Udayana.
The two-fascicle *Āraṇyaka-dhyāna-vidhi-sūtra* is identical in its text to the *Dhyāna-samādhi-sūtra* in the canon. The five-fascicle *Dhyāna-rahasya-uttama-sūtra*...
Upon examining the various collections, the original texts were found to be extremely disordered;
these were not the authentic scriptures and were unfit for circulation.

Although I have searched for the authentic versions of these sutras, they have not yet been obtained. The following nineteen works, such as the *New Practice of the Way* (*Aṣṭasāhasrikā-prajñāpāramitā*), are newly translated.
It consists of forty-two fascicles in total.
Perhaps these are two names for a single scripture,
or perhaps only one scripture was preserved because the original manuscript was unavailable at that time.
The *Dharmābhyudaya-sūtra* (First Principle Dharma Victorious Sūtra), one fascicle; the *Maitreya-bodhisattva-paripṛcchā-praṇidhāna-sūtra*, one fascicle;

the *Bodhicittotpāda-sūtra*, two fascicles, also called the *Dharmapada-śāstra*; the *Saṃgīti-sūtra*, two fascicles, also called the *Collection*; and the *Mahāyānasaṃgraha-bhāṣya*, twelve fascicles—these five works totaling eighteen fascicles were included in the canon according to the Zhou catalog. Although they were recorded twice, only one version is retained today.
The *Ākāśagarbha-paripṛcchā-sūtra* in eight fascicles is the complete single chapter, the "Ākāśagarbha-parivarta," from the *Mahāsannipāta-sūtra*.

The *Ākāśagarbhabodhisattva-paripṛcchā-dhāraṇī-sūtra* in one fascicle is an excerpt from the aforementioned "Ākāśagarbha-parivarta" of the *Tathāgatagarbha-vyūha-rahasya-garbha-sūtra* in two fascicles.
The "Chapter on the Tathāgata’s Nature-Arising" from the old *Avataṃsaka-sūtra*, one fascicle; the *Sukhāvatīvyūha-sūtra* (Sūtra on Rebirth According to One's Vows), one fascicle;
the eleventh fascicle of the *Abhiṣeka-sūtra*; the old *Bhaiṣajyaguru-sūtra*, one fascicle;
the twelfth fascicle of the *Abhiṣeka-sūtra*, titled "The Buddha’s Travel to Vaiśālī"; the *Guhyakapāda-vajrapāṇi-sūtra*, two fascicles; and the *Ekottarika-āgama*, one fascicle.
*The Sūtra on the Seven Courses of Action and Manifest Retribution*, one fascicle; excerpted from the *Ekottarika Āgama*, fascicle 21.
*The Sūtra on the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination*, one fascicle; excerpted from the *Ekottarika Āgama*, fascicle 34.
*The Sūtra on Dharmas Corresponding to the Precepts*, one fascicle; excerpted from the *Ekottarika Āgama*, fascicle 46.
The *Bhikṣu-Questions-to-the-Buddha-on-many-Upāsakas-dying* (一卷), also from the *Saṃyukta Āgama*, fascicle 30;
the *Ekadhanika-Gṛhapati-sūtra* (一卷), from the *Saṃyukta Āgama*, fascicle 30;
and the *Sentient-Beings-Committing-Evil-in-the-Three-Time-Periods-sūtra* (一卷), from the *Āgama*, fascicle 46.
*Chūchōyōkyō*, Scroll Eight; *Shukke Kudoku Kyō* (Sutra on the Merit of Leaving Home), One Scroll.

Recorded as being where the Buddha was at the Karanda Bamboo Grove. The above, from "Kokūzō" (Ākāśagarbha) downwards, is an excerpt from the "Shukke Kudoku-hin" (Chapter on the Merit of Leaving Home) of the *Ken'ugyō* (Sutra of the Wise and the Foolish).
These consist of fifteen sections and twenty-four fascicles.
Since they have emerged from the *Saṃyuktāgama*, they are derivative works.
According to the catalogs of various scriptures,
separately translated texts need not be transcribed; therefore,
they were excluded from the Tripitaka catalogs and not included therein.

The *Makara-matsya-nidāna-sūtra*, one fascicle; the *Venerable Udāyin Leads Various People to Pay Homage to the Buddha and the Saṃgha*, one fascicle; the *Returning to One’s Native Country to Save the Father King*, one fascicle; the *Prince Jalambara*, one fascicle; the *Sūtra on Giving Dharma and Non-Dharma*, one fascicle; the *Sūtra on Teaching and Admonishing Rāhula*, one fascicle; the *Sūtra on the Wheel of Transmigration through the Five Destinies*, one fascicle; the *Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of the Bhikṣu Svāgata*, one fascicle; and the *Sūtra on the Seven Meritorious Deeds with and without Objects*. These nine sūtras, beginning from the *Makara-matsya-nidāna*, are all extracted from the *Mūlasarvāstivāda-vinaya*.

The *Sūtra on the Householder Agnidatta Receiving Retribution*, two fascicles; the *Sūtra of the Venerable Sāriputra and the Pleasant Voice*, one fascicle; the *Sūtra on the Five Kinds of Water Strainers*, one fascicle;
the *Sūtra on the Past Causes and Conditions of Queen Śrīmālā*, one fascicle; the *Sūtra on King Prasenajit’s Faith in the Buddha*, one fascicle;
the *Sūtra on the Retribution for the Slaughter of the Śākya Clan*, two fascicles; and the *Sūtra on the Great Lady Mahāprajāpatī Bhikṣuṇī Entering Nirvāṇa*.

*Jingfa sheshen jing* (Sūtra on Reverently Honoring the Dharma and Sacrificing the Body), one fascicle; *Du er xiejian tongzi deguo jing* (Sūtra on Delivering Two Boys with False Views and Attaining the Fruit), one fascicle;

*Qingjing weiyi jing* (Sūtra on Pure and Austere Deportment), one fascicle—also known as *Xijing damujian shobao jing* (Sūtra on Washing and Purifying: The Retribution Received by Mahāmaudgalyāyana), one fascicle;

*Chu danzheng xian da shuiying jing* (Sūtra on the Great Auspicious Responses Manifested at Birth), one fascicle; *Du jiayuona jing* (Sūtra on Delivering Kātyāyana), one fascicle; *Yiluo po* [fragmentary title].

*The Sūtra on the Karmic Retribution of the Dragon King*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of the Lady Anle*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of Increasing Growth*, one fascicle;
*The Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of Wondrous Light*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra on Subduing Non-Buddhists by Manifesting Great Supernatural Powers*, one fascicle;
*The Sūtra on the Skillful Means of Great Medicine’s Meritorious Deeds*, two fascicles; *The Sūtra on the Buddha Descending from Heaven to Jambudvīpa*, [one fascicle].
*The Sūtra on Crossing over to Śuddhagotamī*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of Hārītī*, two fascicles;
*The Sūtra on the Nun Dharmadinnā Attaining Fruition while Remaining a Laywoman*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra on the Brahmin Vṛkṣaputra and His Arrogance*, one fascicle;

*The Sūtra on Disciples Serving Their Teacher*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra on the Seven Kinds of Non-retrogression*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra on the Buddha Preaching the Abandonment [of Defilements] for a Householder*.

*Yijing* (Miscellaneous Scriptures), one fascicle; *Dìdòng yīnyuán jīng* (Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of Earthquakes), one fascicle; *Sìzhǒng hēibái fǎyìn jīng* (Sūtra on the Four Seals of Black and White Dharmas), one fascicle;

*Fó jiāng rù nièpán dù shànxián jīng* (Sūtra on the Buddha’s Entry into Nirvāṇa and His Deliverance of the Venerable Suvīra), two fasciles; *Fó bānnièpán liǎng dàchén gào wáng jīng* (Sūtra on the Two Ministers Informing the King of the Buddha’s Parinirvāṇa), one fascicle;
*Bādà guówáng fēnshèlì jīng* (Sūtra on the Eight Great Kings Dividing the Relics), one fascicle; *Huoshēng zhǎngzhě xià* (The Householder Huosheng, Part Three), thirty fascicles.
These two sūtras both appear in the *Mūlasarvāstivāda-vinaya-kṣudraka-vastu*. From the "Makara-fish" section downward, there are forty-one sections comprising forty-six fascicles.
These are all narratives of origin (*nidāna*) from the Vinaya of the Sarvāstivāda school,
excerpted and circulated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing;
since they belong to a different category [from the present work], they have not been included here.

The *Māyākāra Ajita Dhāraṇī Sūtra*, one fascicle; the *Ratnagotravibhāga-śāstra*, four fascicles; and the *Ratnakūṭa-sūtra-śāstra*, four fascicles—these three works totaling nine fascicles, beginning with the *Māyākāra*, are all scriptures recorded in the Zhou catalog and currently included in the canon.
I have now searched for the original texts but have not yet obtained them;
therefore, they are not included in this record.
This applies to those newly translated scriptures for which the originals have not been acquired.

I cannot record them in full detail. These include: the *Jingdu sanmei jing* (Sūtra on the Samādhi of Pure Deliverance) in three fascicles; the *Fashu jing* (Sūtra on the Dharma Society) in two fascicles; the *Piluo sanmei jing* (Sūtra on the Vīra-samādhi) in two fascicles; the *Jueding zui fu jing* (Sūtra on the Determination of Sin and Merit) in one fascicle; the *Jiu huo shenming ji ren bing ku e jing* (Sūtra on Saving and Obtaining Life, Relieving People’s Suffering and Calamity) in one fascicle; the *Yiyi jing* (Sūtra on Increasing the Mind) in two fascicles; the *Zuimiaosheng jing* (Sūtra of the Most Sublime and Victorious) in one fascicle; the *Guanshiyin sanmei jing* (Sūtra on the Samādhi of Avalokiteśvara) in one fascicle; the *Qingjing fahang jing* (Sūtra on the Practice of Pure Dharma) in one fascicle; and the *Gao wang guanshiyin jing* (The High King’s Sūtra on Avalokiteśvara) in one fascicle. These constitute ten sections of scriptures totaling fifteen fascicles, beginning with the *Jingdu*.
These are all spurious and suspicious scriptures found within ancient catalogs;
although they were included among the orthodox works in the Zhou catalog,
their literary style and principles both involve human contrivance.
Therefore, these have been excluded from this catalogue and are not recorded herein; in total, there were one hundred and sixteen works in one hundred and forty-two fascicles.
Most of these are found in the currently extant Tripitaka according to various catalogues.
Now, as all these matters are cumbersome and some have been sought but not yet obtained,
I shall not provide a definitive account; fearing that one might not know the details, I will describe them briefly.
If one wishes to know the details of the origins, they are all described extensively in the *Shanfan lu* (Record of the Pruned Compilation).
See *Kaiyuan Shijiao Lu*, fascicle 20; *Lüe chu bielü*, fascicle 4.
